reviews.text: Every 2 seconds there’s an ad about a discount and it’s trying so HARD for me to purchase it. It’s very clear what these people want from me, and I was going to pay for it and see what it was about but they kept SHOVING IT DOWN MY THROAT. reviews.title: Waste of money
reviews.text: There is an ad every 2-3 “lessons” prompting you to “purchase more” even after you are supposedly a “Premium” member. Half the time the recording doesn’t pick up your voice and you have to practically shout at the app. Even if you cancel the subscription the SAME DAY YOU PAY FOR IT, you don’t get a refund, you are out the money you put into it. $150/year is far too expensive for an app that is mostly ads, frustration, and while yes, you are speaking from lesson one, you don’t get pronunciation corrections unless you pay for an additional subscription on top of the $150 a year. Such a scam.

reviews.title: Needs Organizing for Improved Learning
reviews.text: The app is great. I paid as little as I could for a year subscription. But there’s a major issue when wanting to return to what you’ve studied: All your learned words and phrases are in one section. They’re not separated by situations you’d use them in. I wish there were sections for unique scenarios, like being at a restaurant, greeting someone, using polite phrases, etc- or that they were sectioned off at least into their lessons you learn them in; lesson 1, 2, etc. I’ve only got 23 words that I’ve learned so far, and I’ve needed to return the phrases the most, and likely will need to continue returning to that section. Scrolling through everything when it’s not organized could be improved. Since it’s not organized, I have to outsource organizing these phrases to pen and paper. This app could truly be your one and only, all-in-one tool for learning a language, but it still needs that aspect reworked. I hope the developers hear this.

reviews.title: Helps but seriously flawed
reviews.text:
I can say the same exact phrase 3 times in a row, it’ll bust my correct streak which pisses me off then tell me I’m right.  Without changing a thing.

NOTHING is like the advertisement so all of that is false as hell. Maybe if you buy it… then subscribe to more at a weekly rate which is super expensive if you plan to take a few months to learn, it does but, no. It’s just not worth it. Take a Japanese class at a local college, much better bang for the buck. Anyhow, It doesn’t show me any of the Japanese in Japanese, just English and I translate it. Like, show me the hiragana, katakana and kanji so I can learn spelling, sentence structure and writing system along with the spoken word. Instead I get a 1.5 second view of the Japanese as it moves on to the next phrase.

Absolutely not worth the $50 I paid for it, so I canceled but I have it until it expires. I’ll try another app. 

I do not recommend unless you only want to learn basic phrases and do not care to learn the reading and writing to go with it.

Seriously a disappointment for me.

reviews.title: The Falou Ultra ads never stop — AFTER PAYING
reviews.text:
As soon as I paid 50 bucks for a subscription after a pressure sale or they offered me a discount and I impulsively bought it, I heard a terrible AI voice speaking in bad English and mispronouncing the word “Falou” half the time saying FAH-loo and other times saying FAY-low. It’s like an AI grandma character who doesn’t even care enough about her own app to know how it’s pronounced. Ick factor 500.

But that’s not the worst part. After every lesson, they disrupt my immersion with this terrible creepy English to tel me to upgrade to their higher tier paid plan, “Falou Ultra” so I can use their AI chat. I don’t want AI chat, I don’t need AI chat. I have people to practice speaking with in real life. It is disgusting that I cannot turn off these ads, and it is completely ruining the product experience. I already paid $50 and I’m on an annual subscription that renews for a lot more than that. Leave me alone with the ads.

reviews.title: Had potential…
reviews.text: Downloaded Falou as I heard good things about it compared to Duolingo that I felt I wasn’t getting anywhere with it. The first 3 weeks I was quite impressed and had paid for the premium account. After 3 weeks I had a notification saying I needed to delete the app, restart my phone and reinstall the app for me to use it again, after doing this and logging back into my account all my progress had vanished and had to start from scratch learning all the basics again, I contacted customer services who told me I could download their sister app “chats” which would cater to what I’ve already learned on my account, having then downloaded this app, it kept a telling me to go to Falou and I would be notified when my lesson is ready, (also constantly getting notifications saying my lesson is ready but again would tell me to go to Falou) I would then go to Falou but have nothing but issues, the app bugging out, teaching me what I assume was German when I’m trying to learn Italian. I complained to Apple who gave me a full refund. Another downside to the app is it would tell you you’re correct before you even finish the sentence, along with telling you you’re correct even if you make an obvious error, I think you’re better off paying for a premium Duolingo account

reviews.title: Get your wallet out
reviews.text:
I have Duolingo, but I kept seeing this pop-up. It looked really interesting and the fact that you would be able to have real conversations made me think this is probably something I would like. That said, I signed up for, it paid the fee and then found out that if I wanted certain things I had to continue to add more money to their pocket. I was bummed because I REALLY wanted pronounciation help and all of the ads I saw made it look like that was something you would get with this. Not something that you would have to pay separate for. And after that disappointment, I kept getting asked with pop-ups to select other things to pay for… I did not know that with a paid membership I would’ve had to pay for additional things. Duolingo does not do that, once you pay, you have paid.

The popups and extra subscription dollars has ruined this app for me. 

So I paid for it and continue to use Duolingo because at least I’m not getting bombarded with pop ups!

reviews.title: Too reliant on (incorrect) AI
reviews.text:
I like this app as it's very important to practice speaking when learning a new language. However, as Im learning portuguese on it (which i have base knowledge on) i am recognizing incorrect grammar that could seriously mess learners up that don't know better. for example, right now its having me say "eu precisar de comida" which would translate poorly into "i to need food." The correct way would be conjugating precisar into preciso, which is something thats even realized by the ai under the grammar button, but not fixed in the actual lesson. 
Another problem I have with it is that it sometimes asks you to say something that they havent fully taught you how to say yet, so you either have to guess or click "i dont know." It should give a spoken example before doing that. My example is it telling me to say "the telephone is very beautiful" in portuguese, but it hadn't taught how to say "very." with prior knowledge i had assumed it was "muito," but it ended up being "bem" which i wouldnt have known as it didnt tell me it first.
I think this app could be greatly beneficial for language learners that struggle to have conversations, but there is a lot of work that needs to be put into it, rather than sloppy AI, to ensure they aren't being reinforced with incorrect information. Especially!!! seeing as they want you to pay yearly for it.

reviews.title: Cash Grab
reviews.text: After completing a few lessons you hit a wall where it demands payment to continue. The language recognition isn’t great and will reward you for incorrect pronunciations and will register correct pronunciations as wrong. I also have concerns where this teaches you the wrong words for certain scenarios. For example it will ask you questions such as ‘translate Hello, Goodbye’ which in Italian there are a few words for, if you say a correct translation but it’s not the one the computer is looking for specifically it will register a wrong answer, and often the scenarios where that particular word is required doesn’t align with what the computer is looking for, which in the long term would mean it is teaching you wrong. I deleted this app as soon as I hit the paywall. There’s no quick way around learning a language, if you want fluency you have to immerse yourself in it, both through reading, listening & speaking. This app does a good thing with focusing on speaking but I have concerns this app doesn’t have the suitable tech to do this properly. Duolingo is far superior in my opinion, but don’t rely on any app to teach you a language, you have to put the work in beyond what the app puts you through.

reviews.title: Stupid
reviews.text:
Firstly - the price for a year is £20, but you have to click past paywalls one by one reducing it from £100, then to £40, £30
and finally £20 by refusing. Then - it disappear the final price on a 30 min countdown timer in your iPhone’s notch that you can’t turn off, even by turning off notifications. Not only this - voice recognition doesn’t work (it’ll complete exercises as correct before you even say the sentence) and even basic words they don’t distinguish between e.g. in Catalan ‘permís’, ‘amb permís’ and ‘disculpi’ all mean excuse me but are displayed in an incorrect context so you’ll never know how to distinguish and where to place them in a sentence. Awful money-grabbing cheap AI app, deleted

reviews.title: Disappointed
reviews.text: I’ve been using Falou for some time now, and I’m really disappointed. The idea behind the app is good, but the voice recognition has a serious problem. Sometimes I pronounce the wrong word or make a complete mistake, and despite that, the app still marks my answer as correct. As a result, it becomes difficult to know whether my pronunciation is actually good or to learn properly. It’s very frustrating for an app that is supposed to help people improve their language skills. Considering the price, I expected a much more accurate and reliable tool.

reviews.title: Totally disappointed
reviews.text:
I doubted all available 5 stars reviews. I don’t see much difference for the free version and premium version. I paid the annual subscription because I want to have Korean conversations practice with AI. I can’t find it but then it’s comes up ad for Falou Ultra which it didn’t show before and I need to pay more for Ultra..
Moreover, they don’t have lesson topics to choose; also no notes or summary that I learnt or for me to do revision. I can’t even go back to see the previous sentence I learned.   
It’s good to practice the pronunciation at first, but then I found the system sometimes either let me through even not finish speaking the sentence, or not letting me through even I  am sure I speak correctly. Defeat the purpose of correcting my pronunciation and the grammatical mistakes.
I don’t usually pay for the app, but got attracted by the discounted price and the good experience at the beginning. I’m super disappointed now. I would like to have a refund.

reviews.title: I’m suspicious that the 5-star reviews are fake
reviews.text:
This app is so close to being good. I tried using it for Korean and a lot of the sentences are awkward and useless. The speech recognition isn’t very good and I realized it’s because the AI made several pronunciation mistakes (for example pronouncing 시 like “see” and pronouncing 예약 like “이락“). So if I don’t pronounce it the incorrect way the AI wants me to, the AI thinks I’m the one who’s wrong. 
I’m at B1-B2 level and I thought the complexity of the sentences almost right from the beginning was a little ridiculous. There’s no way a beginner could pick this up, but anyone who’s not a beginner can see that it’s full of errors. Another thing that annoys me is that it marks words as “learned” after reviewing them in one session. That’s just not how language learning works.  It just gives users a false sense of accomplishment to keep them hooked. The fact that there’s not even a way to review the individual words outside of the full length sentences tells me this is not a serious language learning app.
